description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.readHeadline: pydantic/pydantic-ai is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: pydantic/pydantic-ai leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: pydantic/pydantic-ai — 6 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 3.1 below its current daily pace, with 9 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 412 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
laude-institute/headlong — No same-day commit after 111 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit whether scheduled OpenWork jobs have an explicit workspace target
dailyInsight.insight: If your OpenWork setup has Automations created before workspace pinning, audit one recurring job: verify whether it records a workspace ID and, if the intended workspace is unavailable, fails visibly rather than running in whichever workspace is currently active.
dailyInsight.mechanism: OpenWork's public main-branch workspace-pinning change carries an optional workspace ID from Automation creation into the desktop runner and cloud executor. The desktop runner selects a present pin and raises an unavailable-runtime error for a missing one; older unpinned assignments keep the active-workspace fallback.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A scheduled agent is an execution commitment, not a continuation of a person's current navigation state. Making its target explicit lets an operator audit where work will occur and turns a silent retarget into a recoverable, visible failure.

actions.audience: OpenWork maintainer or operator who schedules Automations across more than one workspace
actions.label: Trace one Automation's workspace identity
actions.instruction: In a disposable or non-production workspace, create or inspect one Automation and verify that its revision records the intended workspace. Then make that workspace unavailable and confirm the runner reports an unavailable runtime rather than selecting the active workspace. Treat old assignments without a pin as a migration/audit finding, not as evidence that every runner path is protected.
actions.effort: 20-30 minutes in a disposable or non-production workspace

receipts.title: feat(automations): pin Automations to an explicit workspace
receipts.supports: Shows that desktop and cloud Automation execution had used the runner's active workspace, and describes the new revision-level workspace pin and preserved legacy fallback.

receipts.title: Desktop Automation workspace-selection regression tests
receipts.supports: Shows focused public witnesses that a pinned workspace wins over the active workspace and that a missing pin fails rather than silently retargeting the job.

confidence.basis: The public commit narrative, implementation and focused desktop-runner tests agree on the intended placement behavior. The evidence is source and test material, so the action is an audit rather than a claim about a released build or every execution surface.

dailyInsight.limitation: The receipts do not establish that a released OpenWork build contains the change, that all existing Automations have a workspace pin, or that desktop and cloud recovery behavior has been independently verified in a production deployment.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw the call if public source or regression tests show a present but unavailable workspace pin being replaced by the currently active workspace, or if documented behavior says the pin is not carried to an execution path the article names.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for release and migration guidance that lets operators identify legacy unpinned Automations and for end-to-end receipts covering cloud recovery after the target workspace changes.
